title: Pull Requests —

header.html: Follow the GitHub flow; open a pull request with a title, description, reviewers and draft state; review with Comment, Approve and Request changes; update a PR by merging or rebasing main in; choose a merge method and know its effect on history; link issues with closing keywords; clean up branches after a merge; work from a fork
Git 2.50.1 for the local parts; the GitHub documentation (read 2026-11-16) for the GitHub parts

html:
1The GitHub flow and opening a pull request

A pull request (PR) is GitHub's place to propose, discuss, review and merge a change. The figure shows the loop.

The official GitHub flow has six steps:

  1. Create a branch with a short, descriptive name.
  2. Make changes, commit and push.
  3. Create a pull request. A draft is allowed.
  4. Address the review comments.
  5. Merge.
  6. Delete your branch.

The PR adds the conversation, in tabs: Conversation, Commits, Checks, Files changed and Findings (automated results). The merge box lists what still blocks the merge, such as missing approvals.

Field What to write
Title One line that says what changes, like a commit subject
Description What and why, how you tested it, and closing keywords for issues
Reviewers People who know the code; only users with write access can request reviews
Draft For work in progress: it cannot be merged, and code owners are requested only at "Ready for review"

GitHub has two models. In fork and pull, contributors fork the repository and open PRs against the upstream. In a shared repository, collaborators push topic branches to the same repository. Open a draft PR early: the team sees the direction, and nobody reviews unfinished work.

2Reviews and keeping the branch current

A reviewer ends a review with one of three decisions:

Decision Meaning
Comment Feedback without a verdict
Approve The change is good to merge
Request changes The reviewer blocks the merge until the problems are fixed

Anyone with read access can review and comment. Admins can require approvals, and code owners are requested automatically. Requesting a team can notify every member; auto assignment or "Only notify requested team members" reduces the noise. Anyone with write access can dismiss a blocking review if its author is away.

To answer a review, commit on the same branch and push: the PR follows the branch. When main moves on, bring it into your branch in one of two ways.

Way Commands The next push
Merge main in git fetch, then git merge origin/main A plain git push works
Rebase onto main git fetch, then git rebase origin/main Rejected as non-fast-forward, so use git push --force-with-lease

If both sides changed the same lines, Git stops with a conflict. Resolve it locally as in module 4: edit the file, remove the markers, git add, then git commit (merge) or git rebase --continue (rebase). Push afterwards.

Try it. Rebase a PR branch onto the new main, then push it. Your hashes will differ.

git fetch origin
git rebase origin/main
git push
git push --force-with-lease

Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/add-footer.
 ! [rejected]        add-footer -> add-footer (non-fast-forward)
 + aeabac7...b399d7c add-footer -> add-footer (forced update)
Tip

. Use git push --force-with-lease, never plain --force. It refuses when someone else pushed to the branch first.

3The three merge methods and what they do to history

The repository decides which methods are allowed, and merging needs write permission. Here the same three-commit branch is merged three ways into three copies of main.

Method What lands on main Your hashes Local equivalent
Merge commit All PR commits plus one merge commit Kept git merge --no-ff
Squash and merge One new commit with the whole change Gone git merge --squash, then git commit
Rebase and merge The commits one by one, no merge commit New SHAs git rebase, then a fast-forward

Try it. Merge the branch add-cart three ways, each into its own copy of main.

git branch merge-way main; git branch squash-way main; git branch rebase-way main
git switch merge-way;  git merge --no-ff add-cart -m "Merge pull request #12 from ada/add-cart"
git switch squash-way; git merge --squash add-cart; git commit -m "Add cart (#12)"
git switch -c cart-copy add-cart; git rebase rebase-way
git switch rebase-way; git merge --ff-only cart-copy

Now count the result of each way, and look at the merge commit.

for w in merge-way squash-way rebase-way; do
  echo "$w: $(git rev-list --count $w) commits, merges: $(git rev-list --merges --count $w)"
done
git log --oneline --graph merge-way

merge-way: 6 commits, merges: 1
squash-way: 3 commits, merges: 0
rebase-way: 5 commits, merges: 0
*   917291a Merge pull request #12 from ada/add-cart
|\
| * 28d6e12 Add cart tests
| * b1ac790 Add cart total
| * 1ebc4f7 Add cart model
* | e88e34b Add contact page
|/
* 480a0c4 Add README

The merge commit keeps the whole story, and git log --first-parent then reads like a list of PRs. Squash suits short-lived branches, but reusing a squashed branch can cause repeated conflicts. Rebase and merge gives a straight line, but GitHub's rebase always updates committer information, creates new SHAs and drops empty commits.

Try it. The rebased commits keep their subjects but not their hashes.

git log --oneline -3 add-cart
git log --oneline -3 rebase-way

28d6e12 Add cart tests
b1ac790 Add cart total
1ebc4f7 Add cart model
d1add97 Add cart tests
2e4e6cf Add cart total
42776d8 Add cart model

All three ways end with identical files. Only the history differs.

Tip

. After a squash or rebase merge, git branch -d says "not fully merged". Your branch commits are not in main under their old hashes. Check that the change arrived, then delete with git branch -D.

4Linking issues, templates and cleaning up

Closing keywords link a PR to an issue: close, closes, closed, fix, fixes, fixed, resolve, resolves, resolved. Put one in the PR description or a commit message, for instance Closes #10 or Fixes octo-org/octo-repo#100. They are case-insensitive and the colon is optional. They only work when the PR targets the default branch, and merging into it closes the issue. You can also link up to 10 issues by hand in the Development sidebar.

A PR template is a file named pull_request_template.md in the root, docs/ or .github/. Several templates can live in a PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ folder. A template becomes available once it is merged into the default branch.

Clean up after the merge. GitHub shows a "Delete branch" button, and "Restore branch" brings the branch back. Admins can switch on "Automatically delete head branches" in Settings, General, Pull Requests. Then remove the leftovers on your machine.

Try it. Delete the remote branch, then prune a branch that was deleted on GitHub.

git branch -d add-cart
git push origin --delete add-footer
git fetch --prune

warning: deleting branch 'add-cart' that has been merged to
         'refs/remotes/origin/add-cart', but not yet merged to HEAD
Deleted branch add-cart (was 554ece1).
 - [deleted]         add-footer
 - [deleted]         (none)     -> origin/add-title

The warning means the branch matches its remote copy but main lacks its commits: a sign of a squash merge.

A fork is a separate repository with its own branches, issues and PRs; the original is the upstream. Keep it current with git remote add upstream, git fetch upstream and a merge or rebase. The PR branch lives in your fork. The GitHub CLI does PR steps from a terminal (not run here):

Task Command
Open a pull request gh pr create
Merge with a chosen method gh pr merge --squash
Add a PR to the merge queue gh pr merge
Tip

. Write Closes #10 in the PR description, and aim the PR at the default branch. A PR into a release branch will not close the issue.

5Practice Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A three-commit PR is merged with Squash and merge. What does main gain?

  • AThree commits and one merge commit
  • BThree commits that have new hashes
  • COne new commit holding the whole change
  • DOne merge commit pointing at the branch
Show the answer

Answer: C. Squash and merge turns all PR commits into one commit on the base branch.

S2After a squash merge, git branch -d add-cart says the branch is "not fully merged". What is the safest next step?

  • ARun git fetch --prune so that Git then treats the branch as merged
  • BCheck that the change is on main, then run git branch -D add-cart
  • CRun git rebase main on the branch so that its hashes match
  • DRun git push origin --force to mark the branch as merged
Show the answer

Answer: B. The squash commit is new, so Git cannot see the old commits in main; once you confirm the content arrived, -D is safe.

S3A PR says "Fixes #31" but targets release/2.0, which is not the default branch. After the merge, issue 31 is still open. Why?

  • AClosing keywords only work when the PR targets the default branch
  • BThe keyword must be written in capital letters for GitHub to count it
  • CClosing keywords work in commit messages but not in descriptions
  • DThe issue must be assigned to the person who merges it
Show the answer

Answer: A. Closing keywords act only on PRs that target the default branch.

S4Ada rebased her PR branch onto main, and now git push is rejected as non-fast-forward. Which command updates the branch safely?

  • Agit push --force, because a rebase rewrites the branch history
  • Bgit merge origin/add-footer, then a plain git push afterwards
  • Cgit pull to fetch the remote commits, then a plain git push
  • Dgit push --force-with-lease, which stops if someone else pushed
Show the answer

Answer: D. The lease check refuses to overwrite commits you have not seen.

S5Ada opens a draft PR that changes files with a code owner. When will the code owners be requested?

  • AAs soon as she pushes a second commit to the branch
  • BWhen an admin approves the draft PR on her behalf
  • CWhen the PR is merged into the default branch later
  • DWhen she marks the PR as "Ready for review" for them
Show the answer

Answer: D. Code owners are not requested on a draft; marking it ready requests them.

S6A three-commit PR is merged. git rev-list --count main grew by 3, --merges shows 0, and all three hashes changed. Which method was used?

  • AMerge commit, which keeps every commit and adds one more
  • BSquash and merge, which makes one commit from the branch
  • CRebase and merge, which replays the commits on top of main
  • DMerge queue, which tests the PR on its own before it merges
Show the answer

Answer: C. Three new commits with new SHAs and no merge commit is the shape of a rebase merge.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What are the six steps of the GitHub flow?

Show the answer

Create a branch, commit and push, open a pull request, address review comments, merge, delete the branch.

R2What are the three review decisions?

Show the answer

Comment, Approve and Request changes.

R3Which command updates a rebased PR branch safely?

Show the answer

git push --force-with-lease.

R4Which condition must hold for a closing keyword to close an issue?

Show the answer

The PR must target the default branch.

R5Where can the PR template file live?

Show the answer

In the root, docs/ or .github/, named pull_request_template.md.

R6Which two commands delete a branch locally and on the remote?

Show the answer

git branch -d and git push origin --delete.
